topic.angle: 52! is so large that a shuffled deck is almost surely unique

card.title: Your shuffled deck is probably unique

body.claim: Any two properly shuffled decks of 52 cards are almost certain to be in different orders.
body.why: There are 52! ways to order a deck, about 8 × 10^67. With that many possible orders, two properly shuffled decks matching is almost impossible.

probes.question: Roughly how many different orders can a 52-card deck be in?

image_brief.show: A deck of playing cards being shuffled or fanned out

claims.claim: Chance of two proper shuffles matching is effectively zero
claims.quote: it is exceedingly improbable that two randomly selected, truly randomized decks will be the same.

claims.claim: A well-shuffled deck is almost certainly in an order that has never existed before
claims.note: Source speaks of two random decks matching, not of all decks in history. Suggest: 'Any two properly shuffled decks are almost certain to be in different orders.'

claims.quote: There are 52 factorial (expressed in shorthand as 52!) possible orderings of the cards in a 52-card deck.
